scope: Decide how affirmed vowel G40=/y/ participates in adjacent-vowel sequences and whether HNK should license automatic diphthong or glide formation in Y-bearing words. Do not decide lexical stress, G16 romanization, DAYI semantics or L03 curriculum in this gate.
evidence: B1 affirmed G40=/y/ as a vowel distinct from G16=/j/.
B2 affirmed that adjacent vowels, including VVV sequences, are allowed in HNK lexical forms.
FROZEN SARADAYA and TAYOVAN contain A-Y-A and A-Y-O vowel runs under authoritative segment classes.
DAYI is segmentally /d a y i/ and remains without governed whole-word realization.
No recovered governing rule defines diphthongs, glide formation, vowel coalescence or allophony.
Older HOYU metadata that realized Y as /j/ is stale and cannot by itself license automatic /y/ -> /j/.

options.description: In careful/canonical pronunciation, adjacent vowels remain phonologically distinct vowel nuclei unless a later word-specific or sequence-specific rule explicitly licenses another realization. G40 /y/ does not automatically become /j/. Do not establish a productive diphthong inventory yet.
effects: A-Y-I in DAYI is treated as three distinct vowel nuclei for careful pronunciation planning.
A-Y-A and A-Y-O in FROZEN evidence remain legal multi-nucleus sequences.
Phonetic smoothing in fast speech remains future allophony work.

options.description: Author a limited inventory of vowel sequences that behave as diphthongs, including an explicit decision on whether /y/ participates. This would create new phonological structure not recovered from sources and would require sequence-by-sequence evidence/design justification.
Keep legal vowel adjacency from B2 but defer even the careful-pronunciation nucleus policy. This maximizes preservation but blocks reliable whole-word pronunciation and delays B4 stress work.

recommended_rationale: It preserves the affirmed /y/ versus /j/ distinction, fits the stable presence of VVV sequences, avoids inventing an unsupported diphthong inventory, and gives the project a conservative pronunciation baseline without claiming historical recovery.
